meta.description: What is near you right now that you would want to know about? Friends in town, meetups in your languages, local posts — without tracking.
footer.lens: Kafumu is a lens on public, local information. Your location is turned into a coarse #geo cell on your device; coordinates never leave it.
home.finding: Finding your cell… (only a ~5 km area is computed, on your device)
about.title: What is Kafumu?
about.intro: Kafumu answers one question: what is near me right now that I would want to know about? Friends you've met who happen to be in town, meetups in a language you speak or a hobby you have, and what people around here are saying.
about.geo_1: Your device turns your position into the first six characters of its plus code, for example #geo9f469v for central Amsterdam or #geo8ccgqw for Parque das Nações in Lisbon. That is an area of about 5.5 × 5.5 km. Coordinates never leave your device; only the cell does.
about.geo_2: Because a cell is just a word, “what's near me” becomes a hashtag search that works on any network. Add #geo… to a Bluesky post and everyone nearby using Kafumu can see it — no account here needed.
about.private: Private things (people you've scanned, their contact details) stay on your device. Public things live on public networks you control. The Kafumu server keeps only what it must, and most of that expires within days. We can't leak what we don't have.
about.free: Finding people, friends nearby, and hosting meetups will always be free. Kafumu is run by one person; if it helps you meet someone, you'll be able to chip in.

account.title: Your account
account.why: You don't need an account to look around. You need one to host meetups and to have a name others can find.
account.what_we_keep: No email, no phone number. We keep a random id, a hash of your sign-in key, and the name you choose. Delete it any time.

connect.title: Connect
connect.explain: Let someone scan this code with their phone camera. You both keep each other's card — on your devices only.
connect.privacy: The code holds a one-time key. Each person who scans it gets their own private connection; cards travel encrypted and Kafumu's server can't read them.

connect.more_later: You can add WhatsApp, LinkedIn and more on My card later.

profile.title: Be findable
profile.explain: Let people nearby who share a language or interest see you — for a while, in one area. Off by default. Strangers can't message you; they can come and say hi.

home.friends_note: Only people you've connected with can see this, at day and ~5 km precision; the server sees random codes.
patrons.title: Support Kafumu
patrons.intro: Kafumu is built and run by one person, Joop, from Barreiro. There are no investors, no ads that follow you, and nothing to sell about you.
patrons.free: Everything stays free for everyone, forever: finding people, friends around, connecting, signals and hosting meetups. If you can't pay, use it anyway — that's the point. If you can, a little helps it last.
patrons.soon: Ways to chip in are coming very soon. Until then: tell a friend, host a meetup, and send feedback.
patrons.thanks: Supporters get a small cup on their profile and a warm thank-you. No extra features — nobody gets a better Kafumu than anyone else.
cafes.title: For cafés and venues
cafes.intro: Kafumu shows people what's near them that they'd want to know about. When two friends are around, or someone hosts a meetup without a venue, Kafumu can suggest a place to sit. That can be yours.
cafes.point1: Shown only in your area (about 5 km), only to people whose interests match, and clearly labelled.
cafes.point2: No tracking, no cookies following anyone around: matching happens on people's own phones.
cafes.point3: Cheaper than ad networks, and it lands exactly when someone nearby is choosing where to go.
cafes.price: Community and non-commercial events are always free. For venues we're starting simple: a flat price per area per week or month, and the first places for free while Kafumu grows.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Kafumu is built so that we know as little as possible. What we don't have, we can't leak, sell or hand over.
privacy.device: Your cards and personas, the people you've connected with, your notes and tags about them, the keys of each connection, and where you've checked in. None of it is sent to us unencrypted. Your location becomes a ~5 km #geo cell on your phone; coordinates never leave it.
privacy.row_account: Account: random id, a hash of your sign-in key, the name you choose
privacy.row_account_why: To sign you in and show your name
privacy.row_account_kept: Until you delete it; unused accounts are removed
privacy.row_profile: Findable profile (only if you switch it on): languages, interests, one line, where to find you, one area
privacy.row_profile_why: So people nearby can find you
privacy.row_profile_kept: Visible for at most a week; you can hide it any time
privacy.row_meetups: Meetups you host, and a count of who's going
privacy.row_meetups_why: So others can find and join them
privacy.row_meetups_kept: Until a day after the meetup ends
privacy.row_boxes: Encrypted messages between connected phones (cards, signals)
privacy.row_boxes_why: To deliver them; we can't read them
privacy.row_slots_why: So your connections — and only they — can tell you were nearby
privacy.row_logs_kept: As briefly as Google App Engine allows
privacy.never: Your coordinates. Who you're connected with. Your contacts' details. What matched you in your list — that ranking happens on your phone. No third-party trackers, no ad networks.
privacy.caveats: A connect code holds a one-time key in the link; some QR-scanner apps keep a history, so scan with your camera app. Browsers can delete site data (Safari after a week without visits) — install Kafumu to your home screen and keep a backup. Posts you make on Bluesky are public there, not here.
privacy.rights: You can see, export and delete everything we hold about you from your account.
patrons.any_amount: Any amount, once or monthly. PayPal also takes cards without a PayPal account.

badge.explain: A connect code for your badge or T-shirt. It works for two weeks; people who scan it while you're busy are connected next time you open Kafumu.
badge.note: Anyone who sees this code can send you their card — that's the idea. They only get yours when your phone answers.
